change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Operator CAUTION says the Operator fails without rolling-updates; no code does that
findings.body: The CAUTION says that without the `rolling-updates` feature 'the {project_name} Operator will fail'. Nothing in the operator checks the feature. `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` picks the strategy from the CR alone (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:36-42; `UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy` at operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/crds/v2alpha1/deployment/spec/UpdateSpec.java:45-49). The string `rolling-updates` appears only in files of this PR, so a CR with `update.strategy` set and no feature reconciles normally. Reword the sentence to match the behaviour, or add the check if the failure is intended.
findings.originReason: This diff adds the CAUTION block.

verification.reason: `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` picks the logic from `update.strategy` alone, and the only strategy is RECREATE. No operator main code mentions `rolling-updates`, so a CR without the feature reconciles normally. The new CAUTION saying the Operator will fail is inaccurate.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented as a compatibility verdict but is a precondition error
findings.body: Row 4 says 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature rolling-updates is disabled.' The code returns 4 before any compatibility check runs (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-48) and prints an error that the command cannot run. Scripts that branch on 3 versus other codes will read 4 as a tool failure, but the table presents it as an incompatibility result. Describe it as a precondition failure (the command did not run), and consider whether exit 2 ('Invalid CLI option') fits better.
findings.originReason: This diff adds the exit code 4 row and the guard.

verification.reason: `FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) is returned before the config is validated or any compatibility check runs, so 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' wrongly suggests a check took place. Still, the row says the feature is disabled, so the practical impact is small.

findings.title: Same feature guard copied into both update-compatibility commands
findings.body: The four-line guard (check Profile, print the error, `picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)`, return) is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50. `printFeatureDisabled` already lives in AbstractUpdatesCommand (AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85), so a shared guard method there would keep the two in step. Minor.

verification.reason: The same five-line guard (Profile check, `printFeatureDisabled`, `picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)`, return) appears in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. `AbstractUpdatesCommand` already has `printFeatureDisabled`, so a shared guard there is a reasonable minor cleanup.

findings.title: Recreate exit code changes from 4 to 3
findings.body: This brings the code in line with the documented table, which already listed 3 for recreate (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:128-130), so it is a correction. Any script written against the current build's exit code 4 for recreate will change behaviour. The PR body does not mention it; call it out in the description.

contracts.action: check subcommand refuses to run when rolling-updates is not enabled
contracts.before_after: Before: the command ran validateConfig, which checks the --file argument, then compared the metadata. After: when the feature is off it prints an error and exits with 4 before validateConfig, so a missing --file is not reported.
contracts.visible_effect: stderr: 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled.' Exit code 4. Nothing is written.
contracts.failure_mode: In test launch mode picocli.exit does nothing, so the explicit return is what stops the flow. Profile is configured before run() because Picocli.java:128 calls PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers before cmd.execute, and that method calls getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile (PropertyMappers.java:296-306), so the isFeatureEnabled call cannot hit a null instance.

contracts.action: metadata subcommand refuses to run when rolling-updates is not enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/cli/command/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:51-55 and 74-83 (validateConfig, which creates the parent directory of --file, then compatibilityManager.current() and the file write)
contracts.before_after: Before: validateConfig created the output's parent directory and then the metadata was printed and written. After: the guard returns first, so the directory is not created and nothing is printed or written.
contracts.visible_effect: Same error message and exit code 4 as check. No file or directory is created.
contracts.failure_mode: Same as check: the explicit return stops the flow in test launch mode. Profile is initialised before run() as in the check path.

contracts.action: Profile gains the preview feature ROLLING_UPDATES (rolling-updates)
contracts.equivalent_path: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/Profile.java:100 (UPDATE_EMAIL) and :128 (PASSKEYS), same Type.PREVIEW with no dependencies
contracts.before_after: Before: the feature did not exist, so --features=rolling-updates was rejected. After: it is accepted. Under the preview profile it is enabled by default, like the other preview features.
contracts.visible_effect: --features=rolling-updates enables the gate in both update-compatibility subcommands. The preview profile now also enables it. Preview features are logged at INFO when enabled.
contracts.failure_mode: No server code reads the flag, so enabling it changes nothing at runtime beyond the CLI gate.

contracts.action: recreate upgrade exit code changes from 4 to 3
contracts.before_after: Before: a recreate result exited with 4, which contradicted the documented table. After: it exits with 3, matching the table.
contracts.visible_effect: Exit code for an incompatible (recreate) result is now 3. Scripts that matched 4 are affected.
contracts.failure_mode: None in the code. This is a compatibility break for consumers of the preview command, and the PR body does not mention it.

contracts.action: operator CR enables rolling-updates and sets update strategy in the UpgradeTest strategy cases
contracts.before_after: Before: the test set an empty unsupported spec and the update strategy. After: it also sets the feature list, and the UnsupportedSpec import is removed; that type is no longer used in this file.
contracts.visible_effect: The server is started with --features=rolling-updates in the strategy cases. The non-strategy cases are unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: If the stock image was not built with rolling-updates, the start may fail. That depends on how the operator passes features to start, which I did not confirm.
contracts.open_question: Does the server start with --features=rolling-updates on an image built without it? Does the operator start the stock image with --optimized?

contracts.action: custom operator test image built with the feature baked in
contracts.before_after: Before: kc.sh build without features. After: kc.sh build --features=rolling-updates, so the feature is compiled into the image.
contracts.visible_effect: Custom test images accept rolling-updates at start.
contracts.failure_mode: None found in the Dockerfile. The image is only used when a custom image is configured.

contracts.action: docs claim that the operator fails without the feature
contracts.before_after: The CAUTION states a failure. The code selects the strategy from the CR alone, with no feature check.
contracts.visible_effect: The docs tell users that the Operator fails when the feature is off. In practice the Operator reconciles normally.
contracts.failure_mode: Users may enable the feature only to avoid a failure that does not occur.

contracts.action: operator example CR adds spec.features.enabled rolling-updates
contracts.before_after: The YAML key features.enabled matches the FeatureSpec JSON property, so the example is valid.
contracts.visible_effect: The example CR enables the feature.

contracts.equivalent_path: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:8-48 (other macros with the same shape)
contracts.before_after: Before: the macro emitted the command with the user's parameters. After: it also appends the feature flag, so every rendered example includes it.
contracts.visible_effect: Copied examples run the commands with the feature enabled.

summary: No blockers. The new feature gate on both update-compatibility subcommands is wired correctly. Profile is configured before run() (Picocli.java:128), so the isFeatureEnabled call is safe, and both gates return after picocli.exit. Five findings, none above consider or info: an operator doc sentence that claims a failure the code does not produce (advanced-configuration.adoc:449); exit code 4 described as a compatibility verdict when it is a precondition error (update-compatibility.adoc:133); a question whether the UpgradeTest strategy cases can run on the stock image, which lacks the built-in feature and is not gated like the other custom-image tests (UpgradeTest.java:115); a duplicated guard in the two commands; and an info note that the recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, which matches the already-documented table but is not mentioned in the PR body. The base snapshot has no docs/adr directory and no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, so there were no ADR or repository-rule checks to make.

entries.title: Strategy cases enable rolling-updates on an image that may not have it built in
entries.reason: The operator adds `--optimized` only when a custom image is configured or start-optimized is set, and start-optimized defaults to false. With the stock image the server runs a build on startup, so `--features=rolling-updates` takes effect and the start does not fail. With the custom image, the feature is already built in.
